paper.title_en: Entanglement certification and entropy bounds in the asymmetric Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt scenario
paper.abstract_en: Motivated by device-independent quantum information protocols, we study a class of marginal-free asymmetric Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) expressions in which Alice's two measurement settings carry different weights. For <math><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, within the two-qubit projective-measurement model, we derive a tight analytic lower bound on the concurrence of arbitrary two-qubit states compatible with an observed asymmetric CHSH value. We then combine this entanglement-certification result with established entropic-uncertainty, convexification, and Gauss-Radau–Navascués-Pironio-Acín semidefinite-programming techniques to obtain finite-level lower-bound estimates on the conditional von Neumann entropy <math><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>|</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Finally, within the same finite-level semidefinite-programming setting, we compare the entropy estimates obtained from asymmetric and standard CHSH expressions under white-noise and finite-detection-efficiency models. The results indicate that mildly asymmetric choices of <math><mi>α</mi></math> can give more favorable finite-level estimates of the visibility and detection-efficiency thresholds in selected regimes of the models considered here.
